sources.fullCitation: [Report of the Rada Opiekuńcza and the direction of the Szkoła im. Staszica in Warsaw for the school year 1915/16], Przegląd Techniczny 55 (1917), nos. 23 and 24, p. 187. Stowarzyszenie Techników w Warszawie. Biblioteka Cyfrowa Politechniki Warszawskiej.
sources.researchNote: The report states „Rok szkolny 1915/16 rozpoczęto 6 września” and records 128 new candidates across the school, twelve of them in the fifth class, which then held forty-five pupils out of 309 in all. It says that new candidates generally came mostly from Russian state schools and also from provincial schools; Skrynnikov’s school was private. The report does not name the twelve fifth-class entrants or establish Kaper’s individual date of admission or first attendance.

timelineEvents.title: Transfer to the Staszic Real School
timelineEvents.label: 1915/16 · Transfer to the Staszic Real School
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Aged thirteen, Kaper moved from Skrynnikov’s private school to the fifth class of the Staszic Real School, which opened its 1915/16 year on 6 September.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper attended the private school of Aleksander M. Skrynnikov at 49 Żurawia Street, whose curriculum favoured mathematics, the sciences and modern languages over the classical programme of Latin and Greek. Aged thirteen, he transferred to the fifth class of the Stanisław Staszic Real School, which became a state gymnasium in 1918 and where he completed his secondary education. The Staszic school’s report states that its 1915/16 school year began on 6 September 1915 and that twelve new candidates were admitted to the fifth class. It does not name them or establish when Kaper was admitted or first attended. The report says that the new candidates across the school came mostly from Russian state schools; Skrynnikov’s school was private, so this general statement cannot establish Kaper’s individual circumstances. The evacuation of Russian schools and the change of administration in 1915 provide the wider historical context.
